parsed.main_gap: False claim that |E|<|V| forces every component of G to be acyclic; loops/cycles genuinely occur, so the chosen component T need not be a tree.

errors.description: Graph-theoretic step in Lemma 4 is false: a multigraph with |E|<|V| can still contain a cycle or loop (only some component must be acyclic). Concretely, for n=2 with pieces 4u,2u,u and cuts making parts 2u,2u,u,u,u, the top pair {a1,a2} is forced to be a loop at the vertex of the 4u piece, so the component containing vertex n is not a tree and the expansion of Ξ collapses. Repairable in one line (some component is a tree; (3.1) applies to any nonempty J), but as written the argument is invalid.
errors.quote: Since $|E|<|V|$, the multigraph $G$ contains no cycle and no loop: a cycle or a loop through $v$ vertices already uses at least $v$ edges, so a graph containing one would have at least as many edges as vertices, forcing $|E|\ge|V|$ — impossible.

errors.description: Consequent unjustified specialisation: T is taken to be the component containing vertex n and asserted loop-free; this depends entirely on the false acyclicity claim. The correct choice (any acyclic component, which exists by the counting sum|E_C|>=sum|V_C| if all had cycles) is not made.
errors.quote: let $T=(V_T,E_T)$ be the component containing the vertex $n$ (the longest original piece), a simple tree (possibly a single vertex).

parsed.notes: Answer 2^n/(2^{n+1}-1) with correct reduction (Lemma 2), correct cancellation lemma, and a fully correct and rather clever upper-bound construction (Lemma 5). Only the acyclicity step of the lower bound is faulty, and it is repairable in a line.
